title: The Last Hollow Again
premise: Quentin Blackwood, a memory-thief hiding her magic in the anti-magical city of Vell, takes in a feral child named Sable who speaks the First Tongue and carries a fragment of the Hollow—the wound between realms. Hunted by the Wardens who outlawed magic, Quentin discovers Sable is the last living seal of an ancient covenant she herself unknowingly helped break seven years ago. To save the child and both worlds, Quentin must gather the scattered covenant-bearers, confront the Warden commander who was once her found-family brother, and sacrifice her stolen memories to reforge the Hollow—ending with Sable restored, Vell's law rewritten, and Quentin reborn as someone new.
about_author: Mara Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden folklore before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a coastal town where the fog, she insists, keeps its own secrets.

chapters.title: The Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a mud-caked girl appears at Quentin's door speaking a language that makes Quentin's hidden charms hum. The emotional beat is wary tenderness: a woman who trusts no one recognizing something familiar in another abandoned soul.

chapters.title: Charms for a Lawless City
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Flashbacks interweave with a day of selling memory-charms in Vell's black market, establishing how magic was outlawed and what Quentin lost. The beat is quiet dread as Warden patrols tighten and Quentin realizes Sable's presence has drawn attention.

chapters.title: What the Tongue Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Through the child's eyes we see the Hollow: a realm-devouring emptiness sealed by a covenant of five bearers—one already dead. The beat is haunting wonder tinged with terror as Sable begins remembering things no child should know.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A raid on the market forces Quentin and Sable underground, where they find a ledger proving the Wardens' founder helped break the covenant deliberately. The beat is righteous fury hardening into resolve: justice won't come from Vell's law.

chapters.title: Brother Ash
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Warden commander, Dorian—once Quentin's sworn brother in their thief-found-family—is revealed as the covenant-breaker's heir. Their confrontation on a bridge ends in betrayal and escape. The beat is heartbreak: family severed by duty and old wounds.

chapters.title: The Bearer Beneath the Bell
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Quentin and Sable recruit the second bearer, a disgraced bell-ringer who traded his voice for silence. The beat is cautious hope as strangers begin choosing each other—a found family forming around a dying promise.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Stolen Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable touches Quentin's memory-charms and sees the truth: Quentin stole the covenant's keystone memory seven years ago while fleeing Dorian, not knowing what it was. The beat is devastating reckoning—Quentin must face that she broke the world to survive it.

chapters.title: The Hollow Opens
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Hollow breaches Vell; streets dissolve into unmade memory, and the third bearer dies holding the line. The beat is grief-fueled urgency as the remaining bearers race toward the Hollow's edge with time bleeding away.

chapters.title: Covenant of Ash and Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the Hollow's rim, Quentin offers her stolen memories—including every moment with Sable—as the keystone, while Sable speaks the First Tongue to bind it. Dorian, broken by witness, turns his Wardens aside. The climax beat is sacrificial love outweighing identity itself.

chapters.title: The First Morning
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The covenant holds; magic returns lawfully to Vell under a new accord written by bearers, not kings. Quentin remembers nothing but chooses Sable again anyway. The resolution beat is quiet joy: family isn't remembered, it's remade—and this time, freely.
